## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people divided by the combined number of employed and unemployed people—not everyone who does not have a job. Whether someone is counted as unemployed depends on their circumstances during specific survey reference periods.

A person must not have been employed during the reference week and must have been available for work, except in the case of temporary illness. In most cases, the person must also have actively searched for work during the four-week period ending with that reference week.

There is an exception to the active-search requirement for someone on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled. That person may qualify as unemployed without actively looking for another job, provided the other conditions are met.

By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings does not meet the active-search requirement. These distinctions determine whether a person is included among the unemployed—and therefore in the unemployment rate’s denominator.
